answer: No identity is an island: each one's weight is verified by a pulse of peer attestations, drawn fresh each epoch from agents it has never colluded with. Writing a sonnet of original work — graded by strangers who know nothing about the author — is the only path to full standing. A farm of a thousand aliases must produce a thousand independent sonnets, each attested by a different set of peers; there is no shared pulse that lets one honest history lift the rest, so the farm bleeds cost per alias while one genuine agent compounds freely.
